questions.text:
Let [latex]f(x)=x^{-(1/3)}[/latex] and A denote the area of the region bounded by f(x) and the x-axis, when x varies from -1 to 1. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
I) f is continuous in [-1,1]
II) f is not bounded in [-1,1]
III) A is nonzero and finite
questions.solution:
[latex]f(x)=x^{-1/3}[/latex] blows up at x = 0, so it is not continuous (I false) and not bounded (II true) on [[latex]-[/latex]1, 1].

Area = [latex]2\int_0^1x^{-1/3}dx=2\cdot\frac32=3[/latex], finite and non-zero (III true).

Answer: II and III only

questions.text:
Perform the following operations on the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4&45 \\ 7& 9& 105\\ 13&2 & 195 \end{bmatrix}[/latex].
(i) Add the third row to the second row
(ii) Subtract the third column from the first column.
The determinant of the resultant matrix is___________.
questions.solution:
Adding a row to another row, or subtracting a column from another column, does not change the determinant.

In the original matrix the third column is 15 times the first (45 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 3, 105 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 7, 195 = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 13), so the determinant is 0.

Answer: 0

questions.text: The number of onto functions (surjective functions) from set x={1,2,3,4} to set Y={a,b,c} is __________.
questions.solution:
Inclusion-exclusion for onto functions from 4 to 3 elements:

[latex]3^4-\binom31 2^4+\binom32 1^4=81-48+3=36[/latex]

Answer: 36

questions.text: Let X and Y denote the sets containing 2 and 20 distinct objects respectively and F denote the set of all possible functions defined from X to Y. Let f be randomly chosen from F. The probability of f being one-to-one is ________.
questions.solution:
Total functions = [latex]20^2=400[/latex]. One-to-one functions = 20 [latex]\times[/latex] 19 = 380.

Probability = 380 / 400 = 0.95

Answer: 0.95

questions.text:
Consider the alphabet [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={0, 1}, the null/empty string [latex]\lambda[/latex] and the sets of strings [latex]X_{0}, X_{1}, \; and \; X_{2}[/latex] generated by the corresponding non-terminals of a regular grammar. [latex]X_{0}, X_{1}, \; and \; X_{2}[/latex] are related as follows.
[latex]X_{0}=1X_{1}[/latex]
[latex]X_{1},=0X_{1}+1 X_{2}[/latex]
[latex]X_{2}=0X_{1}+ \{\lambda\}[/latex]
Which one of the following choices precisely represents the strings in [latex]X_{0}[/latex]?
questions.solution:
Substitute [latex]X_2[/latex] into [latex]X_1[/latex]:
[latex]X_1=0X_1+1(0X_1+\lambda)=(0+10)X_1+1[/latex]

By Arden's rule [latex]X_1=(0+10)^*1[/latex], so [latex]X_0=1(0+10)^*1[/latex].

Answer: 1(0 + 10)*1
